text: We judge it highly likely that the Velkonian General Staff has completed contingency planning for a limited incursion into the Dravik Corridor and could execute an operation at less than 72 hours' notice. President Malvenko has almost certainly not yet taken the political decision to proceed.

It is likely that Karshevat Metals Group is routing controlled maraging steel to the Norkovan missile programme via its Port Anselm subsidiary, KMG Trading FZE. Shipping records and financial reporting indicate transactions worth at least USD 40 million between March and December 2025, disguised as sales of industrial fasteners.

There is a realistic possibility that the cyber actor we track as KOLVANIR has pre-positioned destructive malware on the networks of at least two Tarvian energy distribution operators. KOLVANIR is almost certainly directed by the Velkonian military intelligence service, the GRD.

We judge it unlikely that the Qeshvari Atomic Directorate will achieve sustained enrichment above 60 per cent at the Marzafan facility before mid-2027. This judgement would change if Qeshvar succeeded in procuring carbon-fibre rotor assemblies abroad; we assess it is actively attempting to do so.

It is highly unlikely that the Morvennite Vanguard currently has the capability to mount a mass-casualty attack outside the Marovel region. The group's intent to strike Western interests is, however, almost certainly undiminished.

It is almost certain that Norkovan gas exports through the Selvane Pipeline fell by more than a third in the first quarter of 2026. Norkovo will probably seek to offset the lost revenue through expanded crude sales carried by its shadow tanker fleet.

We judge it likely that the Velkonian intelligence services will attempt to interfere in Tarvia's presidential election in October 2026, most plausibly through covert financing of the Tarvian Renewal Bloc and inauthentic amplification of divisive narratives online. There is a realistic possibility that such activity would materially affect the outcome in a close race.

We judge it likely that the tanker VARKOSSA (IMO 9938861) conducted a ship-to-ship transfer of sanctioned Norkovan crude off Cape Vestrel on 14 May 2026, her AIS transponder having been disabled for 61 hours. There is only a remote chance that the vessel's declared cargo of gasoil was genuine.
We have high confidence in this judgement, which rests on multiple independent and well-established strands of reporting, including technical collection against the Selvane Pipeline metering system.

We have moderate confidence in our assessment of Karshevat Metals Group's offshore payment flows; reporting is credible but our visibility of the group's banking arrangements in Port Anselm remains incomplete.
We have low confidence in reporting that General Ostrev has been dismissed as head of the GRD; the claim is single-source, uncorroborated, and may reflect deliberate deception.
Our confidence in this judgement is high, although we note a significant intelligence gap on the location of Qeshvar's undeclared stockpile of centrifuge components.
We make this judgement with moderate confidence: our coverage of the Morvennite Vanguard's external operations cell has degraded since the loss of a key reporting stream in late 2025.
We have high confidence that KOLVANIR is subordinate to the GRD's 9th Directorate, based on consistent infrastructure overlaps and corroborating reporting from a reliable liaison partner.

We have low confidence in current estimates of the Velkonian Expeditionary Corps' equipment serviceability rates; the available figures derive largely from Velkonian internal reporting, which routinely overstates readiness.

We judge it highly likely that Drenzel Commodities Ltd (company number 11482956) is acting as a front for the Vokarian state oil trader Nafkor. Since its incorporation on 3 February 2025 the company has reported a single director and no employees, yet declared turnover of £48.2 million in unaudited accounts filed on 30 June 2026, and it chartered four laden tankers from Nafkor-linked owners between May and July 2026.

It is almost certain that the intrusion into Calbright Water's operational technology network on 19 June 2026 was conducted by VORNGLASS, a cyber group subordinate to the Kordunan external intelligence service. The loader, the staging infrastructure and the actor's working hours match those observed in three previous VORNGLASS operations against European utilities.

We assess it is likely that the Tessarine embassy's cultural section is directing the campaign of paid demonstrations outside the Melverton Enrichment Inquiry. Payments totalling £61,400 have passed from Astrelka Media OU to six UK-registered organisers since 12 April 2026.

There is a realistic possibility that the network around Danyal Oreshak will attempt an attack in the UK within the next six months. Oreshak purchased 40 kilogrammes of ammonium nitrate-based fertiliser on 27 July 2026 through a front horticultural business, Ferngale Grounds Ltd, and has conducted reconnaissance of two rail interchanges.

We judge it highly likely that Quolith Precision GmbH is procuring maraging steel for the Velgard Republic's centrifuge programme. The company's order of 18 tonnes from a Rotherham supplier on 9 May 2026, invoiced at £2.3 million, exceeds any plausible requirement of its declared civilian end user.

It is probable that the motor vessel KARNELIS (IMO 9812446) deliberately dragged its anchor across the Selwick interconnector on the night of 2 to 3 August 2026. The vessel slowed to 3.1 knots over the cable route, doubled back once, and its transponder was disabled for 74 minutes at the relevant time.

It is almost certain that the Braykov network laundered at least £210 million through UK cash-intensive businesses between January 2024 and June 2026. Analysis of 14 linked companies shows banking deposits exceeding declared turnover by an average of 340 per cent.

We judge it unlikely that Perrindale Capital LLP was a knowing participant in the Sarventi sanctions-evasion scheme. The firm severed its custody relationship within nine days of the first designation on 21 March 2026 and reported the exposure to OFSI unprompted.

There is a realistic possibility that TIDEMARROW will deploy destructive malware against a UK logistics firm before the end of 2026. Since June the group has staged wiper-capable binaries on three previously compromised networks, a departure from its established ransomware model.

We assess it is highly unlikely that the fire at the Harnwell Ballot Storage facility on 14 May 2026 was directed by a foreign state. Forensic examination attributes ignition to a faulty compressor, and no state-linked actor has shown interest in the site.

There is a remote chance that the self-styled Vanthir Covenant possesses a viable chemical capability. The group's sole procurement attempt, an order of 200 litres of pool chlorinator placed on 8 June 2026, was abandoned at the payment stage, and its self-described chemist has no relevant training.

We judge it highly likely that the Vokarian survey vessel ORLETSA has been mapping seabed infrastructure in the Firthlan Gap rather than conducting the fisheries research declared to the coastal authority. Its track between 11 and 19 July 2026 followed the Norlum gas pipeline for 214 nautical miles with side-scan sonar active.

We judge it likely that the Calvette Line crime group will re-establish its cocaine route through Felderport within three months of the June 2026 seizures, given its retained access to two licensed customs agents.
We assess it is unlikely that the Velgard Republic will conduct a nuclear test before the end of 2027, since tunnel works at Mount Sarvath halted in April 2026 and have not resumed.

It is highly likely that PALEGORSE retains access to at least one UK managed service provider compromised in the September 2025 campaign, notwithstanding the remediation the sector reported complete on 30 January 2026.
It is almost certain that the £34.7 million transferred by Orvath Nominees Ltd to accounts in Sperato between 2 and 6 March 2026 represented proceeds of the Kelbourne pension fraud.

There is a realistic possibility that Tessarine intelligence officers will approach staff of the Aldmere Fusion Consortium at the November 2026 Havrell trade fair, as they did at the two preceding events.
We judge it highly unlikely that Oreshak's network has access to firearms beyond the single deactivated shotgun recovered at Milcote Row on 30 July 2026.

There is a remote chance that operators of the Bravenne shadow fleet will attempt a deliberate grounding in UK waters to obstruct the Selwick approaches; the tactic has been discussed on intercepted channels but never rehearsed.
We assess it is probable that the Braykov network's principal money broker, Ilkan Sevrat, is now operating from Marovel City under an assumed identity first documented on 15 May 2026.

We judge it highly likely that Korvath Freight SA is the central clearing node for Vokarian sanctions evasion in the metals trade. The company, registered in Sperato on 17 October 2024, has invoiced £312 million of nickel and copper cathode shipments to European buyers while holding no warehousing, no vessels and a staff of four. Its bills of lading name three loading ports that customs records show the cargoes never visited, and its settlement bank in Marovel City shares two directors with the designated Nafkor subsidiary Ostrev Trade House. Payments route through a chain of five nominee companies, each dissolved within eight months of formation; the latest, Welleray Commodities Ltd (company number 15733208), applied for strike-off on 29 June 2026, eleven days after its account received £41 million. We expect the network to re-form around a successor vehicle within weeks of any designation. Our insight into the settlement chain rests on a single banking source, and the volume estimate could be understated by a third.

We assess it is likely that VORNGLASS will target the engineering suppliers of UK water utilities over the next six months, in preference to the utilities themselves. Since the Calbright intrusion of 19 June 2026 the group has probed the networks of four firms that maintain telemetry equipment for the sector, including attempts on 7 and 22 July 2026 against Marbeck Controls Ltd using a counterfeit software update signed with a stolen certificate. Supplier networks offer persistent access to several operators at once, and the sector's patching obligations do not extend to third-party maintenance connections. A successful compromise would give the group the means to alter dosing telemetry, although we have seen no intent to cause contamination and judge the sabotage preparations to be contingency work. Our coverage of the group's tasking is indirect, and a shift towards the energy sector, signalled once in April 2026, would shorten the warning we could give.

There is a realistic possibility that the Vanthir Covenant will attempt a marauding attack against a public gathering in the north of England before mid-2027. The judgement rests on the group's shift from online agitation towards physical preparation. Its inner circle of nine, led by Marcus Tellwright, conducted a night exercise on moorland near Gathwaite on 12 July 2026, bought body armour plates through a re-enactment supplier for £3,840 in May, and has twice reconnoitred the Delfringham agricultural show, which drew 34,000 visitors in 2025. Tellwright's writings fix on the show's 2027 date, 22 August, as significant to the group's founding mythology. Recruitment remains slow and two members have withdrawn since June, which may indicate internal doubt about moving to violence. Coverage of the group's encrypted channel lapsed on 4 August 2026; until it is restored, warning of any change in the group's timing would be short.

It is almost certain that the Velgard Republic has resumed production of uranium hexafluoride at the Sarnesk conversion plant. Imagery from 3, 11 and 26 July 2026 shows steam plumes above the fluorination hall, rail tank wagon deliveries on a fortnightly cycle, and the reopening of the plant's dedicated fluorine store, sealed since the Ternhaven Understanding of March 2023. Procurement corroborates the imagery; Quolith Precision GmbH sourced corrosion-resistant valves to a specification matching the plant's original build, and a Velgard front company paid £4.6 million to a Marovel chemicals broker for anhydrous hydrogen fluoride in June 2026. At the observed cadence Sarnesk could convert enough feedstock for a first significant quantity of enriched uranium by late 2027, provided enrichment capacity keeps pace. We cannot yet judge whether the resumption reflects a weapons decision or a negotiating position; the leadership's intent remains the principal gap in our understanding.

We judge it unlikely that the Kordunan navy intends a sustained campaign against UK subsea cables this year, although the capability for isolated attacks is now in place. The auxiliary ORLETSA and the salvage vessel TARNVIK together surveyed some 640 nautical miles of cable route between March and July 2026, and TARNVIK carries a remotely operated vehicle rated to 2,400 metres. Kordunan doctrine treats cable attack as a wartime measure, and both vessels have returned to Port Velsny, where TARNVIK entered refit on 9 August 2026. An isolated deniable strike, of the kind rehearsed against a disused cable off Cape Verlath on 28 June, remains open to them at short notice. The principal uncertainty is decision-making in Velsny rather than capability; failure of the Firthlan fisheries talks, due to conclude on 30 September 2026, would lead us to revisit this judgement, and warning time for a single strike could be a matter of hours.
Zaruvian forces have highly likely committed around 1,800 personnel to the Mordane bridgehead on the River Osk. Resupply depends on two pontoon crossings.
Zaruvia's 3rd Combined Arms Army has advanced up to 4 km towards Brenholt since 12 March. Full encirclement of the city within the next seven days is unlikely.
Zaruvia has almost certainly lost more than 240 main battle tanks since its invasion of Kelnora on 9 February. Around a third were OKV-3s, its most modern in-service type.
The Drayvex Group, a Zaruvian private military company, likely fields around 6,000 contractors in the Ostreth region. Recruitment has slowed since pay arrears emerged in early March.
Zaruvia launched at least 60 Vesk-7 one-way attack UAVs against Kelnoran power infrastructure overnight on 18-19 March. Kelnoran air defences likely downed over 70 per cent.
Zaruvia has removed General Davor Krelin as Joint Force commander after 38 days in post. His dismissal is highly likely linked to stalled progress on the Torvane axis.

The Melst Sea Flotilla dispersed from Port Ruvel after Kelnoran uncrewed surface vessel strikes on 22 March damaged the corvette ZNS Kalvora. An amphibious assault on Port Ilvane is now highly unlikely.
Kelnoran forces have retaken Salvik and advanced approximately 7 km along the Kavessa rail line. There is a realistic possibility Zaruvian units withdraw behind the River Osk within 48 hours.
Zaruvia announced a call-up of 90,000 reservists on 25 March. It is unlikely to train and equip this cohort before June.
Norvex Aeromotiv has almost certainly doubled Vesk-7 production since January, to roughly 900 airframes per month. Kelnoran officials report a 25 per cent failure rate at launch.

The Ostreth Liberation Front has refused to subordinate its 4,000 fighters to Zaruvia's 3rd Combined Arms Army. There is a realistic possibility Zaruvia cuts the group's ammunition allocation in response.
Zaruvia fired 14 Molva-2 short range ballistic missiles in the week to 28 March, its highest weekly total of the war. It is likely expending stocks faster than production can replace them.

Kelnoran deep strikes hit Threl airfield on 30 March, damaging at least five combat aircraft on the ground. Zaruvia will highly likely disperse remaining airframes to bases over 150 km from the front.
Zaruvian casualties since 9 February almost certainly exceed 30,000, including approximately 9,000 killed. Daily rates on the Brenholt axis remain the highest of the war.

Zaruvia is building a second defensive belt 15 km behind the current front line in Ostreth, using an estimated 3,500 troops and contracted labour. The effort likely reflects doubt that the first line can hold.
Spring flooding on the River Osk has cut one of the two pontoon crossings supporting the Mordane bridgehead. There is a realistic possibility the bridgehead becomes unsustainable within seven days.
Zaruvia is highly likely sourcing fibre-optic guidance components through intermediaries in Tolvess. Tolvess customs data shows relevant imports up nearly 300 per cent since December.
A Kelnoran strike near Kavessa on 2 April likely destroyed two Serth-B air defence launchers and an associated radar. Zaruvia has not acknowledged the loss.
Zaruvia retains approximately 1,900 troops in allied Vostrane on Kelnora's northern border. There is a remote chance these forces open a second front before summer.
Zaruvian defence spending will highly likely reach 8 per cent of GDP in 2026, up from 5 per cent in 2025. Plants at Ruvel and Chalsk have moved to three-shift working.
At least 190 personnel of Zaruvia's 44th Air Assault Brigade have surrendered near Salvik since 26 March. Morale in the brigade is likely at its lowest point of the war.
Kelnoran strikes have cut the Kavessa-Threl railway in three places since 1 April. Zaruvia is unlikely to restore full throughput inside two weeks.
Zaruvia has massed an estimated 22,000 personnel and 300 armoured vehicles opposite the Torvane salient. There is a realistic possibility of a renewed push towards Brenholt within ten days.
Zaruvia's stated objective remains full control of Ostreth region by 1 May. At current rates of advance, under 1 km per day, this is highly unlikely.

President Ilo Marset announced a 40,000-strong expansion of Kelnora's territorial defence force on 5 April. Kelnora will almost certainly prioritise air defence interceptors in its next assistance requests.
